title: The compactified distinct-tuple configuration of an affine etale atlas
statement:
Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$, let $X\to B$ be separated of finite type, and let $f:W\to X$ be a representable surjective etale map from an affine scheme of finite type over $B$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $d\geq1$ bound all geometric fibre cardinalities of $f$. Assume that the locus $U\subset X$ of fibres of cardinality $d$ is open and that $W\times_XU\to U$ is finite etale of degree $d$ (its etale-local finite locally free algebra has rank $d$). Choose an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $W\hookrightarrow Y$ over $B$ and a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_B$ into projective space over $B$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] for an integer $m\geq0$. Put $F=W\times_X\cdots\times_XW$ with $d$ factors, and let $V\subset F$ be the complement of the pairwise equality diagonals. Let $Z$ be the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of $V\to Y\times_B\cdots\times_BY$, and let $g_i:Z\to Y$ be its $i$th projection. Then $F$ is an affine scheme, $V$ is a quasi-compact open and closed subscheme of $F$, and $V\to Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion with scheme-theoretically and topologically dense image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. Each $g_i$ is a proper morphism of schemes, and $Z$ admits a closed immersion into a finite projective space over $B$. The open subscheme
$$H=\bigcup_{i=1}^d g_i^{-1}(W)\subset Z$$
is quasi-compact and separated and admits a quasi-compact immersion into a finite projective space over $B$. The maps $f\circ g_i:g_i^{-1}(W)\to X$ agree on overlaps and define a separated finite-type morphism $p:H\to X$. The open $V$ is contained in $H$ and is scheme-theoretically and topologically dense there. The composite $V\to H\xrightarrow{p}X$ factors through $U$ and is surjective onto $U$. For every field $K$ [def-weil-field] and $v\in V(K)$ with image $x\in X(K)$, the $d$ coordinate sections identify $W\times_{X,x}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $\coprod_{i=1}^d\operatorname{Spec}K$; this identification remains true after every field extension of $K$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), proof from the definition of V through the construction of Xprime and its glued morphism, excluding the properness claim and the induction; the coordinate completeness used in the last paragraph.

proof.text: Write $F_r=W\times_X\cdots\times_XW$ ($r$ factors). Start with $F_1=W$. Inductively the projection $F_r\to X$ is representable etale: its projections are base changes of $f$, followed by composition. Apply [lem-trf-space-separated-affine-chart-overlap] to the affine etale charts $F_r,W\to X$ over the affine base $B$. It gives an affine scheme $F_{r+1}$ and a closed immersion $F_{r+1}\to F_r\times_BW$. Induction and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products] give a closed immersion $F\to W^d_B$. This includes $d=1$, when it is the identity. Thus $F$ is affine and quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), the iterated fibre product before defining V

proof.text: Put $R=W\times_XW$. The first projection $R\to W$ is etale, and it is separated since $R$ is affine. Its diagonal section $W\to R$ is therefore open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. For each pair $i<j$, the equality locus in $F$ is the pullback of this section by the $(i,j)$ projection. Closed immersions remain closed under base change, and open subschemes pull back to inverse-image opens. The finite union of these clopen loci is clopen. Its complement $V$ is therefore open and closed in the quasi-compact affine scheme $F$, and is quasi-compact. For $d=1$ the union is empty and $V=F$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), the open and closed diagonals and quasi-compactness of V

proof.text: Put $T=Y^d_B$. The product $W^d_B\to T$ is an open immersion by repeated [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. Combining it with the closed immersion $F\to W^d_B$ of step 1 and the clopen inclusion $V\to F$ shows that $V\to T$ is an immersion: $V$ is closed in $F$, hence closed in the open $W^d_B\subset T$. The given closed immersion $Y\to\mathbf P^m_B$, products of closed immersions, and $d-1$ binary Segre embeddings give a closed immersion $T\to\mathbf P^N_B$ with $N=(m+1)^d-1$. All products and Segre embeddings are over $B$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), the immersion into the product of projective compactifications

proof.text: The closed immersion $T\to\mathbf P^N_B$ makes $T\to B$ proper, hence separated. Since $B$ is affine, $T$ is a separated scheme, and hence quasi-separated. As $V$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $V\to T$ quasi-compact. Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] to this immersion: its canonical factor $V\to Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, scheme-theoretically and topologically dense. The composite closed immersion $Z\to T\to\mathbf P^N_B$ supplies the required projective embedding of $Z$. In particular $Z\to B$ is proper and $Z$ is separated and quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), scheme-theoretic image Z and the dense open immersion V -> Z

proof.text: The given projective embedding makes $Y\to B$ proper. Each projection $T=Y^d_B\to Y$ is a composition of base changes of $Y\to B$ (the identity when $d=1$), hence proper. Its restriction along the closed immersion $Z\to T$ is the proper morphism $g_i$. Put $H_i=g_i^{-1}(W)$. Properness includes quasi-compactness, so the inverse image $H_i$ of the quasi-compact open $W$ is quasi-compact. Thus the finite union $H=\bigcup_i H_i$ is quasi-compact. It contains $V$, since every coordinate of $V$ lies in $W$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), proper projections and the definition of Xprime as the union of their inverse images

proof.text: The open $H\subset Z$ is separated over $B$: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $Z/B$ along $H\times_BH\to Z\times_BZ$. Closed immersions are stable under base change. The same argument over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ shows that $H$ is a separated scheme. Since $H$ is quasi-compact and $Z$ is quasi-separated, $H\to Z$ is quasi-compact. It is an immersion: as $Z\to\mathbf P^N_B$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, $H=Z\cap O$ for an open $O\subset\mathbf P^N_B$, and $H=Z\times_{\mathbf P^N_B}O\to O$ is a closed immersion by base change, followed by the open immersion $O\subset\mathbf P^N_B$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. It is quasi-compact: for any quasi-compact open of projective space its inverse image in $Z$ is quasi-compact, and its further inverse image in $H$ is quasi-compact. This gives precisely the required immersion, without assuming that every open of a quasi-compact scheme is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), H-quasi-projectivity of the constructed open Xprime

proof.text: Restrict the injection $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ to any open $O\subset Z$ containing $V$. On every open $Q\subset O$ it is the same injective map $\mathcal O_Z(Q)\to\mathcal O_V(Q\cap V)$; hence $V$ is schematically dense in $O$. Its topological density restricts as well: every nonempty open of $O$ is a nonempty open of $Z$ and meets $V$. Take $O=H$ and $O=H_i\cap H_j$. In these opens $V$ is still a quasi-compact open immersion, by quasi-compactness of $V$ and quasi-separatedness of the ambient open subscheme of $Z$.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), density in Xprime and the projection overlaps

proof.text: On $O=H_i\cap H_j$ compare $a_i=f g_i$ and $a_j=f g_j$. Both are $B$-morphisms, equal on $V$ because the coordinates of $F$ have the same image in $X$. Their equalizer $E=O\times_{X\times_BX}X\to O$ is a closed immersion by the separated-diagonal hypothesis on $X/B$. Its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ restricts to zero on $V$. Each section of $\mathcal I(Q)$ thus maps to zero in $\mathcal O_V(Q\cap V)$, so the injection of step 7 forces $\mathcal I=0$. The affine quotient description of closed immersions gives $E=O$. Hence the maps agree on overlaps. For a scheme $L\to H$, the inverse images of $H_i$ form a Zariski, hence fppf, covering; the compatible sections of the fppf sheaf $X$ glue uniquely. Uniqueness makes these glued sections functorial in $L$, giving $p:H\to X$ with the required restrictions.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), agreement on overlaps, Tag 084N (lemma-equality-of-morphisms), with its closed-equalizer proof written out

proof.text: The morphism $H\to B$ is finite type: $H\to Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $Z\to B$ is proper, and finite-type scheme maps compose. Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation] to $H\xrightarrow p X\to B$ to obtain local finite type of $p$. The space $X$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal factors as its closed diagonal over $B$ followed by the pullback of the closed diagonal of the affine scheme $B/\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. On affine scheme tests these are closed immersions, and their composite is closed, hence quasi-compact. Now [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applies to the quasi-compact source $H$ and gives quasi-compactness of $p$, hence finite type. Finally $H\to H\times_XH$ is the pullback of the closed diagonal $H\to H\times_BH$. Thus $p$ is separated, with no assumption that $X$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), separatedness and finite type at the beginning of the properness-claim proof

proof.text: For a field $K$ and $v\in V(K)$, put $x=p(v)$ and $P=W\times_{X,x}\operatorname{Spec}K$. It is a scheme etale over $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] it is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions. A $K$-section selects a component and a $K$-embedding of its residue field into $K$, forcing that component to be $\operatorname{Spec}K$ with its unique section. The $d$ pairwise distinct coordinate sections therefore select $d$ different degree-one components. After an algebraic closure of $K$ these already give $d$ distinct geometric points; the assumed upper bound leaves no other components. The coordinate maps give $P\simeq\coprod_{i=1}^d\operatorname{Spec}K$. Base change of this very isomorphism to any extension $K'/K$ gives the last assertion with the same labels.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), the last paragraph: coordinate points are the complete set of inverse images

proof.text: Every geometric point of $V$ has $d$ distinct coordinate points in the fibre of $f$; the upper bound says the fibre has exactly $d$ points. Thus its image lies in the given open $U$, so $V\to X$ factors uniquely through the open subspace $U$ by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Conversely let $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ be a geometric point. The hypothesis that $W_U\to U$ is finite etale of rank $d$ gives a fibre of dimension $d$ over $\Omega$. By the etale-fibre description this is a disjoint union of $d$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, because $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. Enumerate those copies. Their ordered tuple is an $\Omega$-point of $V$ above the chosen point. Hence $V\to U$ is surjective on point classes, as asserted. No nonemptiness of $U$ was assumed or used.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), V surjects onto U in the induction paragraph
